public_rationale: The claim has two parts. On concentration, the Microsoft part holds. Bloomberg, working from Microsoft's FY2026 filing, estimates that OpenAI alone made up about 70% of Microsoft's AI sales (e1). For Amazon and Google, there are only analyst notes that are not public, and UBS's Google figure measures total cloud revenue, not AI revenue (e3). So those two parts cannot be confirmed. On non-disclosure, the claim fails for Microsoft. It disclosed $24.1B of OpenAI revenue in a filing in late July 2026, before this post, and that was reported as the first such disclosure (e1, e2). Microsoft did not state the share of AI revenue, so 'not disclosing that this is the case' holds only in a narrow sense. 'Misleading investors' is a legal and moral judgment, and it is not scored.
limitations: The Microsoft evidence is news reports of a Bloomberg story. The 10-K text itself was not read.
The 70% figure is Bloomberg's estimate, built on an assumed AI revenue total.
Nothing could be checked for Amazon or Google.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast majority of Microsoft, Google and Amazon's AI revenues and revenue growth in their cloud platforms come from Anthropic and OpenAI, and the companies are blatantly misleading investors by not disclosing this.

statement.excerpt: The vast majority of Microsoft, Google and Amazon’s AI revenues and revenue growth in their representative cloud platforms are from Anthropic and OpenAI, and they are blatantly, unashamedly misleading investors by not disclosing that this is the case.

from_speaker: Microsoft, Google and Amazon's AI revenues and revenue growth in their representative cloud platforms
misleading investors by not disclosing that this is the case
73% of AWS' AI revenues, 74% of Microsoft's, and likely 70%+ of Google Cloud's
our_interpretation: The claim has two testable parts. (a) Concentration: for each of the three companies, Anthropic and OpenAI supply well over half of the company's AI revenue (and of the AI-driven growth in its cloud platform), in the period his figures describe, FY2026 for Microsoft and 2026 for the others. Because he relies on analyst estimates, credible estimates count, not only company figures.
(b) Non-disclosure: as of the post date, the companies had not disclosed this concentration to investors.
'Misleading investors' is a normative and legal judgment that cannot be scored. Only the factual non-disclosure part is tested.

'Revenue growth in their representative cloud platforms' is read alongside AI revenue, as in his own figures. His context says the labs drove about 40% of total Azure growth, so 'vast majority' is not applied to total cloud growth.
criteria.support_condition: Credible company figures or estimates show Anthropic and OpenAI supply the clear majority of AI revenue at all three companies, and none of the companies had disclosed this before 2026-08-04.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible figures show the two labs supply well under half of a company's AI revenue, or a company had disclosed its revenue from these labs to investors before the post.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft booked $24.1 billion in revenue from OpenAI during the year to June, Bloomberg reported. The company disclosed the figure in a filing last week. That is most of its AI business. By Bloomberg’s estimate, OpenAI is more than half of Microsoft’s actual AI sales, and probably around 70%.
evidence.explanation: For Microsoft, OpenAI alone is estimated at about 70% of FY2026 AI revenue. Adding Anthropic would only raise that, so the concentration part holds for Microsoft.

evidence.excerpt: It is the clearest picture yet, and the first time Microsoft has spelled the figure out. Investors have pressed the company on exactly this.
evidence.explanation: Microsoft disclosed its OpenAI revenue in a filing in late July 2026, before the 2026-08-04 post. That cuts against the claim that it was not disclosing its dependence on the labs.

evidence.excerpt: According to UBS analyst estimates, OpenAI and Anthropic could account for more than 48% of Google Cloud’s revenue by 2027, up from a projected 27% in 2026.
evidence.explanation: The UBS figures measure the labs' share of total Google Cloud revenue, not AI revenue. They neither confirm nor refute his inferred 70%+ share of Google's AI revenue.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Amazon and Alphabet disclosing revenue from Anthropic and OpenAI, or the analyst notes being published with their figures for AI revenue by customer.
